questions.q: Which stage of the SQL Server Database Administrator career path does this course complete?
options: This course does not belong to any stage of the path
The Advanced SQL Server stage
The Job Ready stage
The Multi-Platform Databases stage
questions.explain: PowerShell, Automation & DevOps for DBAs is the fourth and final course in the Advanced SQL Server stage.

questions.q: Which three courses, alongside this one, make up the Advanced SQL Server stage?
options: Terraform & Bicep and Kafka
Cross-Platform Relational Database Administration and NoSQL/Document & Graph Databases
SQL Server Performance Tuning, SQL Server HA/Backup & Disaster Recovery, and Azure Database Administrator
T-SQL Development, T-SQL for Database Administrators, and SQL Server Database Administration
questions.explain: The Advanced SQL Server stage is Performance Tuning, HA/Backup & Disaster Recovery, Azure Database Administrator, and this automation/DevOps course.

questions.q: What is the next and final stage of the SQL Server Database Administrator path, now that this course is done?
options: Multi-Platform Databases — Cross-Platform Relational Database Administration and NoSQL/Document & Graph Databases
There is no further stage — the path ends here
A second Advanced SQL Server stage covering different topics
A repeat of the Job Ready stage
questions.explain: Multi-Platform Databases is the path's final stage, applying everything built so far to Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Cosmos DB, and Neo4j.

questions.q: What four pieces, built across Lessons 38-41, make up the completed capstone?
options: Only the PowerShell scripts — CI/CD and monitoring were left out of the capstone
A new database engine, a new programming language, a new company, and a new job title
The automation suite, source control + CI/CD, monitoring & alerting, and a story to present it
A GUI dashboard, a mobile app, a chatbot, and a public website
questions.explain: The four connected pieces are the MeridianDBAOps automation suite, source control and CI/CD for schema changes, tuned monitoring and alerting, and the presentation framing from Lesson 41.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a real portfolio version of this capstone include, beyond just the scripts?
options: A list of every dbatools cmdlet that exists, regardless of relevance
A video of every keystroke typed while writing the scripts
Nothing else — the scripts alone are sufficient for a portfolio
A README stating the specific problem, redacted real scripts, rough before/after numbers, and one real pull request or pipeline run
questions.explain: A credible portfolio piece needs a specific named problem, a real before-and-after, and artifacts someone else can actually review — not just code in isolation.
